VBO:0200041.summary: American Cocker Spaniels tend to be merry, even-tempered dogs with a keen inclination to work. They combine considerable speed with endurance in a compact sporting frame, and their traditional flushing role sits alongside their role as companions.
VBO:0200041.shortDescription: A merry, even-tempered American flushing spaniel with endurance and a keen inclination to work.
VBO:0200041.historicalRoots: American sporting spaniel developed for flushing game and companionship.

sources.title: FCI American Cocker Spaniel standard
sources.evidence: FCI 167 utilization: flushing dog and companion. General appearance requires a free, merry dog with keen inclination to work and considerable speed and endurance. Temperament: equable. Colour section defines parti-colour as two or more solid colours, one white, including black-white, red-white, brown-white and roans. Claims apply to the breed, not a purported colour personality.

VBO:0200487.summary: English Cocker Spaniels tend to be affectionate, exuberant dogs whose busy energy comes alive when they follow a scent. Their woodcock-flushing roots help explain the breed’s willingness to push through heavy cover. They emerged as a separate breed from Field and Springer Spaniels after Britain’s Kennel Club was formed in 1873.
VBO:0200487.shortDescription: An affectionate, exuberant English spaniel whose bustling energy comes alive when following scent.
VBO:0200487.historicalRoots: British cocking spaniels used to flush woodcock, recognized separately from Field and Springer Spaniels in the nineteenth century.

sources.title: FCI English Cocker Spaniel standard
sources.evidence: FCI 5 utilization: flushing dog; history derives cocking spaniel from flushing woodcock and records separation from Field/Springer Spaniels after Kennel Club formation in 1873. Temperament: merry, bustling when following scent, fearless of heavy cover, gentle/affectionate and exuberant. Colour section includes blue roan and other roans under particolour/colour varieties. No colour-specific temperament is asserted.

VBO:0200510.summary: Estrela Mountain Dogs tend to be watchful flock guardians, closely attached to the shepherd while wary of unfamiliar people. Their work developed across Portugal’s Estrela Mountains, following herds from the foothills to summer pasture high above the lowlands. Guarding against predators and thieves remains central to the breed’s character.
VBO:0200510.shortDescription: A watchful Portuguese mountain guardian, attached to its shepherd and wary of unfamiliar people.
VBO:0200510.historicalRoots: Long-established livestock guardianship across the Estrela Mountains, including seasonal movement to high summer pasture.

sources.title: FCI Estrela Mountain Dog standard
sources.evidence: FCI 173 explicitly defines long and short coat varieties. Temperament names faithful flock guardian, protective against predators/thieves, distrustful of strangers and docile to master. History documents Estrela foothill-to-summit distribution and summer high pasture after snowmelt. Source character claims apply to both coat varieties.

VBO:0200675.summary: Hovawarts tend to combine an even, confident disposition with protectiveness and strong attachment to familiar people. A good nose supports their use in tracking and rescue as well as watch and guard work. The modern breed was rebuilt from German farm dogs beginning in 1922, carrying forward an older estate-guardian idea.
VBO:0200675.shortDescription: An even, confident German guardian whose good nose also supports tracking and rescue work.
VBO:0200675.historicalRoots: German farm and estate guardians reconstructed as a modern working breed from 1922, with broader utility use.

sources.title: FCI Hovawart standard
sources.evidence: FCI 190 2025 temperament records good nature, even disposition, protectiveness, confidence, good nose, devotion and tracking/rescue/guard utilization. Historical summary starts modern breeding from farm-type dogs in1922. Colour section explicitly recognizes black alongside black-and-tan and blond; it does not assign colour-specific traits.

VBO:0200766.summary: King Charles Spaniels tend to be gentle and affectionate, with a reserved side that can coexist with a happy disposition. These companion spaniels descend from small gundogs later cherished by wealthy owners, and their name remembers King Charles II’s fondness for them.
VBO:0200766.shortDescription: A gentle, affectionate toy spaniel with a reserved side and a long history of close companionship.
VBO:0200766.historicalRoots: English and Continental toy companions developed from smaller spaniel/gundog stock; named for King Charles II.

sources.title: FCI King Charles Spaniel standard
sources.evidence: FCI 128 behavior: happy, reserved, gentle and affectionate. Utilization: companion/toy. History describes smaller gundogs subsequently treasured by wealthy owners and the name’s link to Charles II; distinguishes English Toy Spaniel alias from the related Cavalier. Colour section specifies black-and-tan points.

VBO:0200576.summary: Agile and eager to work, the Schafpudel remains a herding dog especially associated with eastern Germany. Its working drive has also found outlets in dog sports and rescue service. This shaggy regional type belongs to the Old German herding tradition, where flock work is central to its identity.
VBO:0200576.shortDescription: An agile, work-eager regional herder whose flock skills have also found outlets in dog sports and rescue work.
VBO:0200576.historicalRoots: Old German regional flock-working type, especially retained in eastern Germany.

sources.title: GEH — Schaf- oder Hütepudel
sources.evidence: GEH identifies Schaf- or Hütepudel as agile, nimble and eager to work; especially used for herding in the eastern German states, with successful dog-sport and rescue-service work.

VBO:0200798.summary: The Labradoodle’s early story is one of carefully selected guide work. In 1989, Wally Conron crossed a Labrador with a Standard Poodle while seeking a guide dog for a woman in Hawaii whose husband had allergies. Sultan, one of three puppies, was chosen for his temperament and went on to guide her; the cross then found a much wider companion following.
VBO:0200798.shortDescription: A Labrador–Poodle cross with a guide-dog origin story: Sultan was selected for temperament and trained for a woman in Hawaii.
VBO:0200798.historicalRoots: Labrador–Poodle guide-dog breeding at the Royal Guide Dogs Association of Australia in 1989.

sources.title: ABC original Wally Conron / John Gosling interviews
sources.evidence: ABC reports original interviews with breeder Wally Conron and guide-services manager John Gosling: Labrador Brandy×Standard Poodle Harley litter in 1989; Sultan chosen for temperament and sent to guide Patricia Blum in Hawaii. The modern popularity followed publicity for the cross. Claims about Sultan are individual historical facts, not generic temperament predictions.

sources.title: Bryson et al. (2026) — Behaviour in designer Poodle crosses and their parent breeds
sources.evidence: In583Labradoodles, adjusted C-BARQ scores were less undesirable than Poodles for6/12 scales including aggression/rivalry/fear/separation, but more undesirable than Labrador Retrievers for5/12 including rivalry, non-social fear, separation, excitability and trainability. Attachment/attention-seeking, stranger aggression and touch sensitivity showed no difference from either. Mixed comparator-dependent findings do not justify inheriting predictable parental temperament. Existing profile remains individual-scoped guide-work history.

VBO:0200092.summary: Sociable and playful, Australian Labradoodles are bred to engage warmly with people, with lively energy at liberty and a quieter manner when handled. Their development extends beyond a simple Labrador–Poodle cross: approved foundation lines also included water spaniels, retrievers and cocker spaniels. The multigenerational program has its own companion-focused standard.
VBO:0200092.shortDescription: A sociable, playful companion developed through a multigenerational program, lively at liberty and quieter when handled.
VBO:0200092.historicalRoots: Australian multigenerational companion program, incorporating six approved foundation breeds.

sources.title: ALAA — Australian Labradoodle Breed Standard
sources.evidence: ALAA standard describes sociable, comical and joyful temperament, energetic when free and quiet when handled, with friendly approach to people; this is the Australian program’s selected direction, not inferred parental character.

sources.title: ALA — Parent Breeds
sources.evidence: ALA distinguishes Australian Labradoodle development from a simple Labrador×Poodle cross; recognizes Poodle, Labrador, Irish Water Spaniel, Curly Coat Retriever, American Cocker Spaniel and English Cocker Spaniel as the six approved parent breeds, with first standard written in1997.

VBO:0200370.summary: Cockapoos are often affectionate, playful companions with plenty of energy for shared activity. Excitability and difficulty with time apart are also reported in the cross. The Cocker Spaniel–Poodle cross has been known in the United States since the mid-twentieth century. Several cocker types and poodle sizes contribute to today’s dogs, so the name covers a broad range of companion crosses rather than one fixed breed standard.
VBO:0200370.shortDescription: Often affectionate and playful, the Cockapoo is an energetic companion cross with a long-established American history.
VBO:0200370.historicalRoots: Cocker Spaniel–Poodle companion cross known in the United States since around 1950.

sources.title: Cockapoo Club of GB — What is a Cockapoo?
sources.evidence: The Cockapoo Club of GB describes loving, fun and energetic companion character; records United States presence since about1950 and accepts different cocker types, poodle sizes and generations, without one fixed breed standard. No parental temperament is transferred to crossbred dogs.

sources.title: Bryson et al. (2026) — Behaviour in designer Poodle crosses and their parent breeds
sources.evidence: In1856Cockapoos, adjusted C-BARQ scores were more undesirable than Poodles on6/12 scales and Cocker Spaniels on10/12. Excitability and separation-related problems were higher than both comparators. Aggression/fear/rivalry comparisons also differed, whereas attachment/attention-seeking and touch sensitivity showed no significant difference from either. Supports caution about excitability and time apart; does not negate club-reported affectionate/playful character or predict each dog.

VBO:0201045.summary: Playful and affectionate, Pomskies are bred for close companionship and can approach new people with curious interest. The emerging cross began attracting breeders around 2012, pairing Siberian Husky and Pomeranian lines. Some programs now include American Eskimo ancestry as they work toward a more consistent companion type; an occasional alert bark or howl remains part of the picture.
VBO:0201045.shortDescription: A playful, affectionate emerging companion cross, with curious social interest and sometimes an alert bark or howl.
VBO:0201045.historicalRoots: Emerging Siberian Husky–Pomeranian companion cross, with some club programs adding American Eskimo ancestry.

sources.title: APKC — Standards2025
sources.evidence: APKC2025 standard describes affectionate and playful human companionship, sociability and curiosity, with an alert bark or occasional howl; these are documented emerging-program ideals, calibrated as tendencies. Records initial Siberian Husky/Pomeranian cross and later American Eskimo use in some programs.

sources.title: APKC — History of the Pomsky
sources.evidence: APKC history reports Pomsky breeding appearing around2012 and later program expansion; warns against pure Husky puppy photographs mislabeled as mature Pomskies. Describes American Eskimo addition in participating club lines.

VBO:0200066.summary: Anglo-Français de Petite Vénerie join a pack readily and bring courage, persistence and an active searching style to the trail. Their fine nose, carrying voice and endurance have made them valued hounds for following hare and fox, continuing a French working tradition shaped by crossing native hounds with English stock.
VBO:0200066.shortDescription: A tenacious French pack hound with a fine nose, a carrying voice and a tradition of following hare and fox.
VBO:0200066.historicalRoots: French hare-hunting packs developed from French and English hound crosses; breed club founded in Poitiers in 1978.

sources.title: Société de Vènerie: Anglo-Français de Petite Vénerie
sources.evidence: Société de Vènerie breed account describes pack-oriented character, active search, courage, tenacity, fine nose, voice, endurance and hare/fox work; expressly notes variation through selection and training.

sources.title: FCI325: Anglo-Français de Petite Vénerie
sources.evidence: FCI325 distinguishes the exact medium-sized Anglo-Français de Petite Vénerie and supplies head, ear, body, coat and tail morphology.

VBO:0200165.summary: Biewer Terriers keep a playful, whimsical manner into adulthood and may trot around carrying a favorite toy. Breed founders describe a strong attachment to their owners and bursts of excited running. Gertrude and Werner Biewer founded the breed in Germany in the 1980s, before later enthusiasts established breeding programs in the United States.
VBO:0200165.shortDescription: A playful German toy terrier known for staying whimsical into adulthood and carrying a favorite toy.
VBO:0200165.historicalRoots: German breeding program of Gertrude and Werner Biewer in the 1980s.

sources.title: AKC: Biewer Terrier
sources.evidence: AKC breed profile explicitly describes whimsical attitude retained into adulthood and carrying toys.

sources.title: AKC: Biewer Terrier history and founder interview
sources.evidence: AKC history interviews US breed founder Gayle Pruett about owner attachment, childlike behavior and zoomies; identifies Gertrude and Werner Biewer and their German 1980s origins.

VBO:0200946.summary: Norman Artesien Bassets are outgoing, affectionate hounds whose patient trail work has a melodious soundtrack. They follow a line steadily rather than quickly, hunting alone or in a pack. Their short legs let them enter dense vegetation that larger hounds cannot reach, especially in pursuit of rabbits, their traditional favorite quarry.
VBO:0200946.shortDescription: An affectionate, outgoing French basset that follows rabbit trails patiently, giving a melodious voice.
VBO:0200946.historicalRoots: Controlled French basset breeding from the 1870s; Basset Artésien Normand name adopted in 1924.

sources.title: FCI34: Basset Artésien Normand
sources.evidence: FCI34 describes outgoing and very affectionate temperament, excellent nose and melodious voice, slow persistent tracking, rabbit preference and dense-vegetation access enabled by short legs.

VBO:0200942.summary: Griffon Nivernais bring courage and initiative to difficult scent trails, with a marked taste for rough ground and thickets. Their working style favors staying power over speed, and they can be independent or obstinate. Recreated in the Nivernais region during the late nineteenth century, they remain associated chiefly with wild-boar hunting in small packs or alone.
VBO:0200942.shortDescription: A courageous, independent French griffon that persists through rough ground and thickets on scent trails.
VBO:0200942.historicalRoots: Recreated in the Nivernais region in the late 19th and early 20th centuries with Vendéen, Foxhound and Otterhound contributions.

sources.title: FCI17: Griffon Nivernais
sources.evidence: FCI17 directly describes courage, initiative, occasional independence/obstinacy, difficult terrain and thickets, endurance rather than speed, chiefly boar hunting and late 19th/early 20th recreation history.

VBO:0200559.summary: Gascogne Braques Français tend to be gentle, responsive pointers with a close attachment to their people. In the field, the larger Gascogne type usually searches less widely than its Pyrenean relative and alternates trot with gallop. French kennel-club accounts emphasize a cooperative working manner, a fine nose and willing retrieval rather than speed alone.
VBO:0200559.shortDescription: A gentle, cooperative French pointer whose measured field search alternates trot and gallop.
VBO:0200559.historicalRoots: Large Braque Français type of southwest France, separately standardized from the smaller Pyrenean type.

sources.title: SCC: Braque Français commented standard
sources.evidence: SCC commented standard pages4–7 describes close human attachment, gentle/docile temperament, training responsiveness and retrieval. Page5 distinguishes Gascogne’s closer search and alternating trot/gallop from the faster Pyrenean type.

sources.title: FCI133: Gascogne Braque Français
sources.evidence: FCI133 exact Gascogne morphology and southwestern origins; tail generally docked, long or naturally short also accepted. Current original has visibly docked short tail; do not call it natural bobtail.

VBO:0200297.summary: Catahoula Bulldogs are working crosses selected for stamina and persistence in farm, guarding and hunting tasks. They combine American Bulldog and Louisiana Catahoula Leopard Dog ancestry, with parent proportions that can change across generations. The name covers a developing working type with considerable individual variation in temperament and appearance.
VBO:0200297.shortDescription: A variable American Bulldog–Catahoula cross developed for persistent farm, guarding and hunting work.
VBO:0200297.historicalRoots: American working cross of Louisiana Catahoula Leopard Dog and American Bulldog, including later-generation breeding.

sources.title: CPR Kennel Club: Catahoula Bulldog standard
sources.evidence: CPR registry’s exact Catahoula Bulldog standard identifies the hybrid parentage, first-generation50:50 and later75:25 proportions, stamina/perseverance and farm, guard and hunting roles. Broad suitability promises omitted; no claim all individuals share a temperament.

VBO:0008017.summary: The Gorbeiakoa Basque Shepherd tends to be self-confident, sociable and even-tempered, with a strong inclination to herd. Its pastoral work calls for gathering a flock without biting, responding to the shepherd’s signals and returning to the handler, skills tested in the RSCE’s breed aptitude trial.
VBO:0008017.shortDescription: A self-confident, sociable Basque herder, with a balanced temperament and a strong pastoral instinct.
VBO:0008017.historicalRoots: Basque pastoral working dog; the RSCE maintains separate Gorbeiakoa and Iletsua variety standards.

sources.title: RSCE Gorbeiakoa Basque Shepherd standard and aptitude trial
sources.evidence: RSCE Gorbeiakoa temperament: typical herding disposition, self-confident, sociable and balanced. Utilization: herding. Aptitude trial tests entering and gathering sheep without biting, stopping at the handler’s direction and returning to the shepherd. This is a description of working goals and documented tests, not a promise about any individual. Gorbeiakoa standard has distinct red-fire coat, fine long muzzle, medium drop ears and body length/height about1.1.

VBO:0201094.summary: Pugs tend to be even-tempered companions with a happy, lively disposition, combining an air of dignity with an alert intelligence. Their history reaches from China to Europe with Dutch traders, and they were admired in the Netherlands by the 1500s. Fawn dogs were the familiar English type before a black pair arrived in 1877.
VBO:0201094.shortDescription: A happy, lively companion with a dignified streak, whose history reaches from China to Europe.
VBO:0201094.historicalRoots: Chinese companion dog brought to Europe by Dutch East India Company traders; established in England in fawn before black dogs arrived in1877.

sources.title: FCI Pug standard
sources.evidence: FCI253 gives origin China; companion utilization; behavior great charm, dignity/intelligence and even-tempered happy/lively disposition. History records Dutch traders, Netherlands1500s, English fawn population until1877 when black pair introduced. Color section explicitly accepts fawn. No fawn-specific temperament is claimed.

VBO:0200640.summary: Griffon Belge dogs tend to be alert, watchful companions, closely attached to their people and balanced in temperament. Their roots lie in the small rough-coated dogs of Brussels, once used to guard carriages and keep stables clear of rodents. Royal interest helped these Belgian dogs spread abroad around 1900.
VBO:0200640.shortDescription: An alert, watchful Belgian companion, closely attached to its people and rooted in carriage and stable work.
VBO:0200640.historicalRoots: Small Brussels rough-coated Smousje descendants used to guard carriages and clear stable rodents; promoted by Belgian royal interest around1900.

sources.title: FCI Griffon Bruxellois, Griffon Belge, Petit Brabançon standard
sources.evidence: Joint FCI80/81/82 standard describes all three as balanced, alert, proud, very attached to owner and watchful. History names Brussels Smousje ancestors, carriage-guarding and stable rodents, and Queen Marie-Henriette’s interest leading to popularity/export around1900. FCI81 Griffon Belge is rough-coated black or black-and-tan; distinct from red Griffon Bruxellois and smooth Petit Brabancon. No coat-specific temperament invented.

VBO:0201011.summary: Petit Brabançons tend to be proud, alert little companions, watchful and strongly attached to familiar people. They share the Brussels stable-dog ancestry of the rough-coated Griffons, where guarding carriages and hunting rodents were everyday tasks. Nineteenth-century Pug and toy-spaniel crosses helped shape the smooth-coated type.
VBO:0201011.shortDescription: A proud, alert Belgian companion, watchful and devoted, with roots in Brussels carriage and stable work.
VBO:0201011.historicalRoots: Smooth-coated member of the small Belgian dog family derived from Brussels Smousje; nineteenth-century Pug and Ruby King Charles crosses helped fix type.

sources.title: FCI Griffon Bruxellois, Griffon Belge, Petit Brabançon standard
sources.evidence: Joint FCI80/81/82 standard describes balanced, alert, proud, very attached owner and watchful temperament. History names rough Brussels Smousje, carriage/stable rodent work, and19thcentury Ruby King Charles/Pug bloodlines producing short black coat/fixing modern type. FCI82 Petit Brabancon distinguished by short harsh flat coat, rather than rough beard. No independent unsubstantiated temperament difference from rough Griffons asserted.

VBO:0200549.summary: The French Tricolour Hound follows big-game trails by scent as part of a working pack. Its living tradition is rooted in French hunting kennels: at Haut Poitou, these hounds work alongside Poitevins in a deer-hunting tradition that has continued for more than a century in the forests of Poitou.
VBO:0200549.shortDescription: A French pack hound still used alongside Poitevins in the old deer-hunting tradition of Haut Poitou.
VBO:0200549.historicalRoots: French large pack-hound tradition, including the Haut Poitou deer-hunting kennel in the Moulière forest.

sources.title: FCI219: Français Tricolore
sources.evidence: FCI219 identifies this exact French Tricolour identity as a pack hound for big-game hunting. It provides morphology but no breed-specific household temperament, so none is invented.

sources.title: Société de Vènerie: Haut Poitou and Hardouinais kennel accounts
sources.evidence: Société de Vènerie describes the Haut Poitou kennel and its more-than-century deer-hunting tradition in Poitou forests; explicitly identifies the two breeds currently there as Poitevin and Français Tricolore. The age belongs to the hunting tradition, not a claim that this exact breed existed throughout.

VBO:0200627.summary: Great Gascony Blues tend to be calm, readily directed hounds with a strong instinct to work in a pack. A fine nose and deep, resonant voice accompany methodical, persistent trail work. This large Gascony hound traditionally follows big game, while some work alone as tracking hounds; its strength is staying power rather than speed.
VBO:0200627.shortDescription: A calm Gascony pack hound whose fine nose, deep voice and methodical trail work favor staying power.
VBO:0200627.historicalRoots: Traditional large scenthound of Gascony and southern France, used in packs and individually on trails.

sources.title: FCI22: Grand Bleu de Gascogne
sources.evidence: FCI22 directly states very fine nose, deep sonorous howling voice, intent hunting, instinctive pack behavior, calm temperament and easy response to orders; utilization includes big game/hare and individual tracking.

sources.title: Société de Vènerie: Grand Bleu de Gascogne
sources.evidence: Société de Vènerie describes calm/easy direction, methodical and tenacious work, deep resonant voice, endurance rather than pace, pack work or individual lead tracking. No household suitability or individual guarantee is added.

VBO:0201154.summary: Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonkas are cheerful, affectionate companions that tend to stay closely involved with their people. They learn readily and may announce a visitor with a bark before settling again. The breed took shape in postwar Leningrad, where enthusiasts developed a small companion dog for apartment life.
VBO:0201154.shortDescription: An affectionate Russian companion that learns readily and tends to stay closely involved with its people.
VBO:0201154.historicalRoots: Postwar Leningrad companion-dog breeding; the Russian colored lapdog took shape during the 1950s and 1960s.

sources.title: AKC: Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka character and history
sources.evidence: AKC breed account describes cheerful/sociable and affectionate character, enjoyment of human company, intuitive learning, alert barking followed by settling and development by postwar Leningrad enthusiasts for apartment life. Individual tendencies, not promises, are stated.

sources.title: AKC official Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka standard
sources.evidence: AKC official breed standard approved2021/effective2023 describes small sturdy slightly longer-than-tall body, dropped ears, beard/moustache, very wavy or curly dense coat and full undocked tail curled over back; solid fawn allowed, parti/merle/solidwhite excluded.

VBO:0200411.summary: Miniature wire-haired Dachshunds share the breed’s friendly, even temperament and persistent enthusiasm for following a scent. Their hunting ancestry includes work below ground, but Dachshunds also flush game and track wounded animals above it. This bearded miniature belongs to one of nine size-and-coat varieties.
VBO:0200411.shortDescription: A friendly, persistent miniature scent hunter, with a wiry beard and the Dachshund’s versatile working roots.
VBO:0200411.historicalRoots: German Dachshund working ancestry below and above ground; three documented sizes and three coat varieties.

sources.title: FCI148 Dachshund standard, published25May2021; English edition14March2022
sources.evidence: FCI148 behavior describes friendly, even temperament and passionate, persistent, fast hunting with an excellent nose. History: known since Middle Ages; short-legged dogs selected from Bracken for underground work; versatility above ground giving tongue, flushing and tracking wounded game; Deutsche Teckelklub founded1888. Three sizes and three coats give nine varieties. These general Dachshund traits apply across documented varieties; no unsupported size/coat-specific temperament is asserted.

VBO:0200414.summary: Rabbit long-haired Dachshunds carry the breed’s friendly, steady character alongside a determined interest in scent. Dachshunds developed from short-legged hunting dogs that could work underground, then became versatile trackers and flushers above ground too. The rabbit is the smallest of the three sizes in the German standard.
VBO:0200414.shortDescription: A friendly, determined little scent hunter: the smallest Dachshund size, carrying the long-haired coat.
VBO:0200414.historicalRoots: German Dachshund working ancestry below and above ground; three documented sizes and three coat varieties.

sources.title: FCI148 Dachshund standard, published25May2021; English edition14March2022
sources.evidence: FCI148 behavior describes friendly, even temperament and passionate, persistent, fast hunting with an excellent nose. History: known since Middle Ages; short-legged dogs selected from Bracken for underground work; versatility above ground giving tongue, flushing and tracking wounded game; Deutsche Teckelklub founded1888. Three sizes and three coats give nine varieties. These general Dachshund traits apply across documented varieties; no unsupported size/coat-specific temperament is asserted.

VBO:0200419.summary: Standard long-haired Dachshunds tend to be friendly and even-tempered, with a keen nose and the persistence of a working hunter. Their ancestors were selected for underground work, while the breed also became a versatile flusher and tracker above ground. Germany’s Deutsche Teckelklub has supported Dachshund breeding since 1888.
VBO:0200419.shortDescription: A friendly, persistent scent hunter with a flowing coat and a working history above and below ground.
VBO:0200419.historicalRoots: German Dachshund working ancestry below and above ground; three documented sizes and three coat varieties.

sources.title: FCI148 Dachshund standard, published25May2021; English edition14March2022
sources.evidence: FCI148 behavior describes friendly, even temperament and passionate, persistent, fast hunting with an excellent nose. History: known since Middle Ages; short-legged dogs selected from Bracken for underground work; versatility above ground giving tongue, flushing and tracking wounded game; Deutsche Teckelklub founded1888. Three sizes and three coats give nine varieties. These general Dachshund traits apply across documented varieties; no unsupported size/coat-specific temperament is asserted.

VBO:0200420.summary: Standard smooth-haired Dachshunds combine a friendly, balanced disposition with a passionate interest in scent and a persistent hunting style. The breed has been known since the Middle Ages, developing from short-legged hounds selected for work underground. Its repertoire also includes flushing and tracking above ground.
VBO:0200420.shortDescription: A friendly, balanced scent hunter whose determined working style reaches above and below ground.
VBO:0200420.historicalRoots: German Dachshund working ancestry below and above ground; three documented sizes and three coat varieties.

sources.title: FCI148 Dachshund standard, published25May2021; English edition14March2022
sources.evidence: FCI148 behavior describes friendly, even temperament and passionate, persistent, fast hunting with an excellent nose. History: known since Middle Ages; short-legged dogs selected from Bracken for underground work; versatility above ground giving tongue, flushing and tracking wounded game; Deutsche Teckelklub founded1888. Three sizes and three coats give nine varieties. These general Dachshund traits apply across documented varieties; no unsupported size/coat-specific temperament is asserted.

VBO:0200421.summary: Standard wire-haired Dachshunds share the breed’s friendly, even temperament and keen interest in scent. Persistence matters in a dog developed to work below ground, yet Dachshunds also hunt while giving voice, flush game and follow wounded animals. The wiry coat is one of three coats bred across three recognized sizes.
VBO:0200421.shortDescription: A friendly, persistent scent hunter, with a wiry jacket and versatile working roots above and below ground.
VBO:0200421.historicalRoots: German Dachshund working ancestry below and above ground; three documented sizes and three coat varieties.

sources.evidence: FCI148 behavior describes friendly, even temperament and passionate, persistent, fast hunting with an excellent nose. History: known since Middle Ages; short-legged dogs selected from Bracken for underground work; versatility above ground giving tongue, flushing and tracking wounded game; Deutsche Teckelklub founded1888. Three sizes and three coats give nine varieties. These general Dachshund traits apply across documented varieties; no unsupported size/coat-specific temperament is asserted.
